content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

I want a rectangular box that is 220mm wide, 300mm long and 160mm high. Let it be on the upside open and have walls with 8mm thickness and a 12mm thick bottom. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step procedure (only words, no execution yet)

1. Decide a common reference point.  
   • Put the exterior box’s lower-left-front corner at the global origin (0 ,0 ,0).  
   • All subsequent block coordinates are stated relative to that origin.

2. Create the exterior solid.  
   • Call functions.block with  
     – x_size = 220 (overall width)  
     – y_size = 300 (overall length)  
     – z_size = 160 (overall height)  
     – x, y, z = 0 for the basepoint  
     – subtraction = False (this is the first, additive volume)

3. Remove the interior cavity to form the open box.  
   • Compute the inner clear dimensions by subtracting twice the wall thickness from width & length, and the bottom thickness from height:  
     – inner width = 220 – 2·8 = 204 mm  
     – inner length = 300 – 2·8 = 284 mm  
     – inner height = 160 – 12 = 148 mm  
   • The cavity’s basepoint must sit 8 mm in from every side wall and 12 mm above the global origin so the 12 mm-thick bottom stays: basepoint = (8, 8, 12).  
   • Call functions.block a second time with  
     – x_size = 204  
     – y_size = 284  
     – z_size = 148  
     – x = 8, y = 8, z = 12  
     – subtraction = True (this block is removed from the first one)

4. There are only these two blocks; no further geometries are required.

When you say “prepare the function call,” I will format one single functions.block call containing both blocks (as parallel arrays) that executes the steps above, and then await your explicit go-ahead before dispatching it.

Now i want you to execute the prepared function calls one after the other. If you need to do some calculations or geometrical algebra, use the CreateCode Function first. Execute the first prepared function call. Submit all required variables at once
